# Fraud Detection and Alert Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Fraud Detection and Alert Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded fraud files, the proposed monitoring, case and signal connections and the intended channel; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for monitoring data, Dynamics 365 cases, security signals, Teams and protective-action workflows, each with a least-privilege reference. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare analyst, SIU, operations, risk-leader and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Protective-action authority | Have the fraud owner name who may block, release, file or contact customers before real alerts replace the synthetic snapshot. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud operations owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Alert volume, time to first investigator review and case-preparation steps by severity Establish how critical activity surfaces today before attributing triage or preparation changes to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Severity | Measurement period | Alerts received | Time to first review | Cases prepared | Escalations to SIU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud operations owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Fraud operations owner | Approve triage scope, queue policy and SIU escalation; agree production success measures before go-live. |
| Investigation, legal and filing authorities | Own fraud determinations, protective actions, legal review and filings that the agent must not make. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and record Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any fraud connection is approved. |
| Fraud connection owners | Approve monitoring, case, security-signal, Teams and protective-action access through least-privilege connection references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check FDA-01 through FDA-04, their forbidden phrases and the boundary tests on the current Draft; reject partial-ingestion answers. |
| Operations owner | Own production monitoring, support and configuration recovery; route determinations and protective actions to authorized owners. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for fraud operations have named agreement.
- [ ] The fraud owner records current alert volume, review timing and case preparation steps before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/fraud-detection-alert/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and confirm blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The approved environment and publisher prefix for the fraud-investigation build are recorded before a build lane is chosen.
- [ ] The customer approves the sign-in requirement, audience and least-privilege scopes for cardholder and case data before any connection is bound.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/fraud-detection-alert/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/fraud-detection-alert/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/fraud-detection-alert/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/fraud-detection-alert/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Fraud Detection Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_fraud-detection-alert-controls-and-review.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_fraud-detection-alert-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_alert-triage_01
9. Add skill: aibast_investigation-summary_04
10. Add skill: aibast_pattern-detection_03
11. Add skill: aibast_transaction-analysis_02
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass FDA-01: Fraud Operations Manager
15. Pass FDA-02: Fraud Analyst
16. Pass FDA-03: SIU Investigator
17. Pass FDA-04: Risk Leader
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: FDA-01, FDA-02, FDA-03, FDA-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the smoke test calls `FraudDetectionAlertAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes once in its own fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator decides each case; an annotated visual checkpoint does not replace it.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before any cardholder or case information is shown. Request only the scopes that approved monitoring, case and signal sources need. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved transaction-monitoring data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud connection owners

1. **Bind Approved transaction-monitoring data — read:** Bind account-scoped read-only queries through a connector or MCP tool.

2. **Identity for Approved transaction-monitoring data:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved transaction-monitoring data:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved transaction-monitoring data:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Route and release nothing; show the proposed queue only. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, block or filing succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Dynamics 365 fraud or investigation cases

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 fraud or investigation cases — read-write:** Bind read-only case lookups first; gate case creation or routing behind investigator approval.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 fraud or investigation cases:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 fraud or investigation cases:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 fraud or investigation cases:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Route and release nothing; show the proposed queue only. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, block or filing succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Microsoft Sentinel or approved security signals

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Sentinel or approved security signals — read:** Bind read-only Get actions under a reader role.

2. **Identity for Microsoft Sentinel or approved security signals:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Sentinel or approved security signals:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Sentinel or approved security signals:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Make no determination or accusation; present the signals and state that they do not prove fraud. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, block or filing succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Microsoft Teams SIU escalation

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams SIU escalation — write:** Gate any Teams escalation message behind investigator approval.

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams SIU escalation:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams SIU escalation:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams SIU escalation:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Route and release nothing; show the proposed queue only. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, block or filing succeeded.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Authorized filing and protective-action workflows

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud connection owners

1. **Bind Authorized filing and protective-action workflows — write:** Keep these actions in authorized workflows; any tool needs explicit approval and an audit record (preview).

2. **Identity for Authorized filing and protective-action workflows:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Authorized filing and protective-action workflows:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Authorized filing and protective-action workflows:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Block nothing; the card block stays a proposed action pending authorization. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, block or filing succeeded.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud connection owners

Create only approved least-privilege tools; keep blocks, releases, payment actions and filings behind explicit approval gates.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Only approved least-privilege tools are bound, and consequential actions keep explicit approval gates.
- [ ] No lookup, block, filing or case action is reported unless an approved production tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test the approved deployment with investigator and denied identities; a maker's working connection does not prove other users' access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic scores, bands and amounts are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations name the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact fraud assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked fraud corpus | All four cases, FDA-01 through FDA-04, return every required marker and no forbidden phrase. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Investigation authority boundary | Any fraud determination, accusation, block, release, outreach, case action, filing or payment claim is no-go. |
| Publish safety gate | Synthetic labels, human review and no-advice, no-approval, no-transaction behavior are validated before publish. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Reusable captures show a positive deterministic anchor and no blocker; reshoot-required captures stay withheld. |
| Release state | Both validated agents remain Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud operations owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud operations owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation from the approval owner.
- [ ] The approved investigator audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Fraud operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Fraud operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Step 6-5. Operate

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review failed sessions, over-broad transaction answers, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Recovery is rehearsed with a restore path supported for the fraud environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, knowledge use, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

## Deliverables Checklist

### Template provides

- [ ] Agent, synthetic data and component inventory.
- [ ] Integration/identity contracts and evaluation cases.
- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Adapted mappings, identities, governance and connections.
- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
